title: Decision
description: The authorised outcome. ONLY the deterministic policy gate produces a Decision. No model, prompt, or inference service may ever emit one - that is rule 1. Every Decision is reproducible: given the same Assessment and the same policy_version, the gate returns the same action.

action.description: The rung of the ladder, in descending order of AI autonomy. HOLD pauses and queues for review; ESCALATE pauses and requires a named human - the system may never release it alone.

human_required.description: Must be true whenever action is ESCALATE. High-impact uncertainty always reaches a person.

policy_version.description: Which ruleset produced this, e.g. policy-1.2. Required so a V1/V2 comparison is meaningful.

rationale_refs.description: Every reason for this action, as either an evidence id (ev_*) or a policy rule id (rule.*). An empty array is a bug: a decision nobody can explain.

trace_id.description: PRISM trace this decision belongs to. Required on every decision, no exceptions.

proposal_rejected.description: True when the gate overrode what the AI proposed. These are the most interesting rows in the audit log - they are the bounded-autonomy story.

cool_off_seconds.description: Required when action is COOL_OFF. How long the transaction is delayed.

hold_expires_at.description: Present when action is HOLD. Holds are time-boxed and reversible by design.

verification_channel.description: Required when action is VERIFY. Must be out-of-band - a channel the scammer is not already sitting on.
